answer: An agent economy can require a locked bond for every identity before it may earn fees for updating a shared atlas of lotus habitats. Rewards depend on verified updates, so a new identity alone adds no useful signal. Running 1,000 fake agents requires 1,000 bonds, each locked for 30 days. This makes a sybil swarm costly: the attacker must tie up capital for every account, sacrificing liquidity even if the accounts earn nothing.
